bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds (Rs 93 Cr) allocated: Rs 12.5 Cr working capital by Mar’26, Rs 17.5 Cr capex by Mar’27, rest in FDs; no dividend policy yet; priority is growth, geographic expansion, and tech R&D; future dividends to be considered post-growth phase
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Government payment delays (mitigated by milestone billing and DPR-stage urgency); land acquisition protests delaying timelines; competitive bidding pressure in geospatial; reliance on government infrastructure spending; execution risk in new international markets
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, optimistic, and focused on execution; emphasized technology as a structural differentiator; acknowledged private sector growth potential but prioritized government projects; transparent on IPO fund deployment; no overpromising on guidance
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The Rs 88 Cr of unutilized IPO proceeds are held in fixed deposits (classified under other current assets), not idle cash; digital twin R&D investment (Rs 130 Cr advance) is a strategic bet to capture future government digital infrastructure mandates; 60-65% revenue is recurring from government clients, indicating sticky relationships
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- IPO cash explicitly positioned as a growth cushion (equipment purchase, hiring, expansion) to be deployed without adding further debt.
- GMR Engineering Services, the acquired target, was debt-free, and the acquisition was funded via a fixed AUD cash consideration rather than raising incremental borrowing.
- Selective, capability-additive M&A (the GMR deal cited as a template) is framed as an ongoing capital-deployment strategy alongside organic reinvestment.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated single-vendor delivery model: survey, LiDAR mapping, design, land acquisition support and project management under one roof, which reduces the number of vendors a client must coordinate and keeps accountability with one consultancy.
- Breadth of technical staff - over 710 engineers, surveyors, planners and geospatial specialists working across Indian and international technical standards and moving between design, client engagement and field execution.
- Digital survey technology - LiDAR-based corridor mapping, drone surveys, Bridge Information Modelling (BrIM) and traffic analytics that improve survey accuracy, shorten design timelines and reduce downstream rework.
- Shift from data capture to data analysis: combining spatial datasets with in-house modelling and AI-based feature extraction to support corridor alternatives, land and environmental impact assessment and regulatory submissions.
- Long execution track record across greenfield and brownfield projects, including a national rail footprint spanning multiple railway divisions and zones, and a willingness to take on assignments other firms turn down.
- Multidisciplinary urban team - planners, transport engineers, GIS specialists, economists and social development experts within a single team - matched to how urban problems present themselves.
- Accreditation stack including a NABL-accredited geotechnical laboratory, ISO 27001 and CMMI Level 3.
- Largely debt-free balance sheet.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Execution risk - the most immediate risk in the business — A delay in survey mobilisation, a hold-up in statutory approval, a subcontractor missing a milestone, or a land access dispute can each affect billing schedules and working capital independently of whether the underlying engineering is sound. The exposure is less about whether projects eventually get delivered - they generally do - and more about whether delays erode margin along the way.
- Concentration risk across clients, geographies and service lines — Specialised consultancies build depth in a small number of sectors or client relationships, and that depth is where the exposure sits: a business weighted too heavily toward a narrow set of public agencies, geographies or service lines is vulnerable to slower tender cycles. Presence across rail, roads, geospatial, water, environmental services and urban planning is stated to reduce this in practice.
- Regulatory and compliance risk, including listed-SME obligations — Tender rules, environmental clearances, land documentation and client-specific technical standards each carry their own compliance burden, and as a listed SME the Company also carries disclosure and governance obligations a private company of the same size would not. Compliance must be checked at contracting and at each project milestone rather than reviewed retrospectively once delivery has been affected.
- Dependence on specialised technical talent and attrition — The business depends on specialised technical staff, and attrition affects delivery continuity more than it would in a less specialised business. Training, retention incentives and documented handover processes are the stated mitigants on the talent side, and staff retention over the long term is described as central to the delivery model given the field conditions and client relationships infrastructure consulting requires.
- Technology dependence, data integrity and cyber security — Growing reliance on LiDAR, UAV survey equipment, GIS platforms and mobile mapping systems introduces dependence on system uptime, data integrity and cyber security that did not exist to the same degree five years ago. System redundancy and access controls are the stated mitigants.
- Project-based revenue and milestone billing driving working-capital cycles — Risk exposure follows from the nature of the business - project-based revenue, milestone billing and dependence on statutory approvals - and revenue recognition and working-capital cycles in engineering consulting carry genuine complexity, which is why the reliability of financial reporting depends directly on the internal financial control environment.
- Unreconciled counterparty balances flagged by the statutory auditor — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to balances of advances from clients and amounts due from sundry debtors being subject to confirmation and reconciliation, and likewise for advances to vendors and balances outstanding in sundry creditors. The opinion is not modified in respect of these matters.
- Unutilized IPO proceeds pending deployment — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter notes unutilized IPO proceeds of Rs. 66.43 Crores as at March 31, 2026 temporarily invested pending utilization, leaving the return on a material part of the raised capital dependent on future deployment.

business.body:

business.body:

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Monarch Surveyors and Engineering Consultants Limited is an infrastructure consultancy that delivers end-to-end solutions across transportation, urban planning, environment, water and industrial sectors, rendering services from topographic survey up to Project Management Consultancy for multidisciplinary infrastructure projects. Its clients are Indian government institutions, road authorities, railways, municipal bodies and private entities, in India and overseas. The integrated delivery model brings engineering survey, DGPS and LiDAR mapping, geotechnical investigation, GIS and geospatial services, structural design, environmental and social impact assessment, land acquisition support, traffic studies and project management into a single structure, so clients deal with one accountable consultancy rather than coordinating several specialist vendors.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Railways:** Corridor and alignment planning, Final location surveys, Detailed engineering, Bridge and structure design, OHE and signalling layouts, GAD/ESP preparation for bridges and stations, DPRs for freight yards and terminals, Geotechnical investigation
- **Roads and Highways:** Master planning, Feasibility studies, Engineering surveys, Geotechnical investigations, Land acquisition support, Detailed project reports, Structural design, Traffic modelling, Project management
- **Geospatial:** Aerial and drone-based LiDAR, Mobile LiDAR, Terrestrial laser scanning, High-resolution GIS mapping, AI-based feature extraction, Digital twins, Land record digitisation
- **Urban Planning and Design:** Master planning, Transit-oriented development, Land-pooling schemes, 3D city modelling, Smart-city integration, Project management support

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Focus on upstream, integrated mandates where Monarch's digital depth can command a premium, rather than competing on scale with larger domestic and global consultancies.
- Expand into higher-margin, technology-driven design and lifecycle consulting work, shifting the revenue mix away from pure survey hours toward higher-yield, platform-based engineering and data services.
- Run the verticals - railways engineering, roads and highways, urban planning and GIS, water and environmental engineering, geospatial and LiDAR, project management consultancy, and buildings and structural engineering - as a single platform rather than independent businesses.
- Own the full data lifecycle by holding fixed-wing LiDAR systems and drone fleets in-house, from capture through processing to delivery, reducing dependence on third-party providers.
- Deploy technology that shortens turnaround - Trimble GEDO CE 2.0 trolley systems for railway track geometry audits, MX-9 mobile mappers on highways, and standardised GIS workflows - so the Company can bid competitively for government contracts that carry penalty clauses for delay.
- Move the Geospatial division from an internal support function to a standalone business segment, delivering GIS and BIM outputs through web-based platforms rather than as fixed deliverables.
- Build recurring revenue by structuring field data collection as a subscription-based asset management service for municipal bodies and commercial developers, a more durable model than project-based survey work.
- Address working-capital stress by tightening milestone terms on new contracts and expanding the private-sector client base.
- Invest in talent - headcount growth plus training on updated digital tools - to relieve the scarcity of BIM specialists, drone pilots, geospatial analysts, hydrologists and sustainability experts that constrains how much work can be taken on.
- Longer-term development priorities centre on sustainable construction and green surveying practices, combining high-resolution terrain analysis with hydrological modelling so developers can cut earthwork volumes and material waste at the design stage.
- Use the national presence established with July 2025 IPO capital to extend beyond the earlier regional base.
- Near-term focus on technology investment, talent development and disciplined execution, as larger and more complex projects push clients to consolidate survey, design and regulatory work with fewer firms that deliver an integrated package.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: This bundle carries almost no company-level capex or capacity narrative; its expansion content is largely the macro infrastructure backdrop rather than Monarch's own build-out. What the Company itself discloses here is inorganic and capability expansion rather than physical capex. Subsequent to the close of the financial year, Monarch completed the acquisition of GM & FE Ryan Pty Ltd, Trustee of GMR Engineering Services Unit Trust, Australia, on fulfilment of the agreed conditions precedent, execution of the definitive transaction documents and receipt of the requisite statutory, regulatory and corporate approvals; the entity became a wholly owned subsidiary after March 31, 2026, and the acquisition is described as a material corporate development expected to strengthen the Company's international presence and engineering capabilities. Equity shares were listed on the SME Platform of BSE Limited on July 29, 2025, and the Board states the Company is currently actively expanding across all verticals and is strategically positioned to accelerate its growth trajectory. Capability expansion is people- and skills-led: more than 12,000 hours of training were conducted in FY26, aimed squarely at keeping technical staff current on GIS, BIM and drone survey methods. The demand backdrop cited for this expansion includes the Union Budget 2026-27 raising infrastructure spending by 11.4% to Rs. 12.2 lakh crore (approximately 3.2% of GDP), a Bharatmala programme of approximately 34,800 km of national highway development, a PPP pipeline of 13,400 km at an estimated cost of Rs. 8.3 lakh crore over the next three years, 35 multimodal logistics parks representing approximately Rs. 46,000 crore of investment in development, and airport growth from 74 in 2014 to around 164 in 2025 under the UDAN scheme. No plant, site, capacity or rupee capital-expenditure quantum for the Company is disclosed in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's infrastructure cycle has moved from periodic capex spurts to a sustained, policy-backed build-out; what matters for Monarch is the proportion of that spend passing through upstream, knowledge-intensive services - surveys, DPRs, geospatial intelligence, design and project management.
- Union Budget 2025-26 raised capital expenditure to Rs. 11.21 lakh crore, or 3.1% of GDP, and public capex has grown from approximately Rs. 2 lakh crore in FY15 to over Rs. 12 lakh crore in FY27 (BE).
- CRISIL projects nearly Rs. 143 lakh crore of infrastructure spending between FY24 and FY30, more than double the preceding seven years, with roughly Rs. 36.6 lakh crore earmarked for green investment.
- Roads and highways account for the largest near-term pipeline: MoRTH has outlined a PPP programme of approximately 13,400 km at an estimated cost of Rs. 8.3 lakh crore over the next three years, alongside 35 multimodal logistics parks under PPP involving around Rs. 46,000 crore of investment.
- Rail and metro will continue to generate demand for corridor planning, geotechnical work, final location surveys and multimodal integration, supported by near-complete electrification and continued investment in new lines, capacity augmentation, safety works and high-speed corridors.
- Urban infrastructure is under increasing pressure from mobility demand, water supply, drainage and land-use planning, driving investment in GIS-based planning, transit integration and network upgrades.
- Water and energy programmes generate steady demand for hydrology, network design, environmental and social impact studies and climate-resilient engineering, driven by flooding risk, wastewater regulation and renewable energy integration.
- GIS-led planning frameworks are pushing India to conceive infrastructure as interconnected networks rather than standalone assets, so corridor studies now combine urban impact, land systems, environmental and social assessment within a single scope - favouring firms that can combine surveys, design, geospatial intelligence, ESG and regulatory support in one delivery framework.
- PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan funding drove a significant share of this year's project awards, and those awards have grown more technically demanding.
- Mix shift: revenue is moving away from pure survey hours toward higher-yield, platform-based engineering and data services; revenue from operations grew 11.39% for the year ended 31 March 2026.
- Water Solutions work has moved from asset-mapping and localised pipe-routing toward river-basin modelling and coastal erosion infrastructure design, with margins in the segment holding up well; standardisation of GIS workflows cut manual data-processing time by 40%, freeing senior engineers for higher-value hydraulic advisory work.
- In the Energy segment, regulatory clearance is usually the more time-consuming element of an assignment rather than the engineering itself.
- Personnel costs rose in the near term to support the technology transition, but the same transition has reduced dependence on manual labour, which is expected to support operating margins over the medium term.
- Working-capital stress: debtor turnover extended to 113 days during the year, reflecting the billing cycles typical of public-sector contracts.
- The market the Company addresses is expected to reach USD 10.29 trillion by 2034 (7.02% CAGR), drawing in more competitors - domestic and larger global consultancies - all investing in LiDAR, digital twins and AI-based analytics; Monarch's constraint is scale rather than technical capability, since larger competitors can price more aggressively, absorb project delays more easily and invest faster in new technology.
- Talent is a second constraint: demand for BIM specialists, drone pilots, geospatial analysts, hydrologists and sustainability experts is outpacing supply, which directly affects how much work the Company can take on and deliver well.
- Land delays, environmental approvals, financing gaps and talent scarcity are described as real headwinds.
- Transportation (railways and highways) remains the principal segment, accounting for approximately 48% of the active order book - nearly half the order book in rail and highways.
- Secured a Rs. 13,000 lakh Northern Railway rate contract spanning 36 months, for engineering surveys and land acquisition management.
- Land acquisition and design consultancy for the Somnath-Dwarka Expressway packages in Gujarat exceeded Rs. 10,000 lakh in aggregate value.
- Undertook project management services for the upgrade of the Ghorpadi (Pune) and Wadi Bunder (Mumbai) depots under the Vande Bharat network.
- The Company's position going into FY27 rests on the order book, technical capability and balance sheet strength.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

currentContext.business: Monarch Surveyors and Engineering Consultants Limited is an infrastructure consultancy that delivers end-to-end solutions across transportation, urban planning, environment, water and industrial sectors, rendering services from topographic survey up to Project Management Consultancy for multidisciplinary infrastructure projects. Its clients are Indian government institutions, road authorities, railways, municipal bodies and private entities, in India and overseas. The integrated delivery model brings engineering survey, DGPS and LiDAR mapping, geotechnical investigation, GIS and geospatial services, structural design, environmental and social impact assessment, land acquisition support, traffic studies and project management into a single structure, so clients deal with one accountable consultancy rather than coordinating several specialist vendors.

Railways: GAD/ESP preparation for bridges and stations

currentContext.expansion: This bundle carries almost no company-level capex or capacity narrative; its expansion content is largely the macro infrastructure backdrop rather than Monarch's own build-out. What the Company itself discloses here is inorganic and capability expansion rather than physical capex. Subsequent to the close of the financial year, Monarch completed the acquisition of GM & FE Ryan Pty Ltd, Trustee of GMR Engineering Services Unit Trust, Australia, on fulfilment of the agreed conditions precedent, execution of the definitive transaction documents and receipt of the requisite statutory, regulatory and corporate approvals; the entity became a wholly owned subsidiary after March 31, 2026, and the acquisition is described as a material corporate development expected to strengthen the Company's international presence and engineering capabilities. Equity shares were listed on the SME Platform of BSE Limited on July 29, 2025, and the Board states the Company is currently actively expanding across all verticals and is strategically positioned to accelerate its growth trajectory. Capability expansion is people- and skills-led: more than 12,000 hours of training were conducted in FY26, aimed squarely at keeping technical staff current on GIS, BIM and drone survey methods. The demand backdrop cited for this expansion includes the Union Budget 2026-27 raising infrastructure spending by 11.4% to Rs. 12.2 lakh crore (approximately 3.2% of GDP), a Bharatmala programme of approximately 34,800 km of national highway development, a PPP pipeline of 13,400 km at an estimated cost of Rs. 8.3 lakh crore over the next three years, 35 multimodal logistics parks representing approximately Rs. 46,000 crore of investment in development, and airport growth from 74 in 2014 to around 164 in 2025 under the UDAN scheme. No plant, site, capacity or rupee capital-expenditure quantum for the Company is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.risk: Execution risk - the most immediate risk in the business
risks.note: A delay in survey mobilisation, a hold-up in statutory approval, a subcontractor missing a milestone, or a land access dispute can each affect billing schedules and working capital independently of whether the underlying engineering is sound. The exposure is less about whether projects eventually get delivered - they generally do - and more about whether delays erode margin along the way.

risks.risk: Concentration risk across clients, geographies and service lines
risks.note: Specialised consultancies build depth in a small number of sectors or client relationships, and that depth is where the exposure sits: a business weighted too heavily toward a narrow set of public agencies, geographies or service lines is vulnerable to slower tender cycles. Presence across rail, roads, geospatial, water, environmental services and urban planning is stated to reduce this in practice.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk, including listed-SME obligations
risks.note: Tender rules, environmental clearances, land documentation and client-specific technical standards each carry their own compliance burden, and as a listed SME the Company also carries disclosure and governance obligations a private company of the same size would not. Compliance must be checked at contracting and at each project milestone rather than reviewed retrospectively once delivery has been affected.

risks.risk: Dependence on specialised technical talent and attrition
risks.note: The business depends on specialised technical staff, and attrition affects delivery continuity more than it would in a less specialised business. Training, retention incentives and documented handover processes are the stated mitigants on the talent side, and staff retention over the long term is described as central to the delivery model given the field conditions and client relationships infrastructure consulting requires.

risks.risk: Technology dependence, data integrity and cyber security
risks.note: Growing reliance on LiDAR, UAV survey equipment, GIS platforms and mobile mapping systems introduces dependence on system uptime, data integrity and cyber security that did not exist to the same degree five years ago. System redundancy and access controls are the stated mitigants.

risks.risk: Project-based revenue and milestone billing driving working-capital cycles
risks.note: Risk exposure follows from the nature of the business - project-based revenue, milestone billing and dependence on statutory approvals - and revenue recognition and working-capital cycles in engineering consulting carry genuine complexity, which is why the reliability of financial reporting depends directly on the internal financial control environment.

risks.risk: Unreconciled counterparty balances flagged by the statutory auditor
risks.note: The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to balances of advances from clients and amounts due from sundry debtors being subject to confirmation and reconciliation, and likewise for advances to vendors and balances outstanding in sundry creditors. The opinion is not modified in respect of these matters.

The auditor's Emphasis of Matter notes unutilized IPO proceeds of Rs. 66.43 Crores as at March 31, 2026 temporarily invested pending utilization, leaving the return on a material part of the raised capital dependent on future deployment.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Monarch is an end-to-end infrastructure consultancy that takes roads, rail, water and urban projects from topographic survey through to project management consultancy, delivered by a team of over 710 engineers, surveyors, planners and geospatial specialists.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Monarch Surveyors and Engineering Consultants Limited is an infrastructure consultancy that delivers end-to-end solutions across transportation, urban planning, environment, water and industrial sectors, rendering services from topographic survey up to Project Management Consultancy for multidisciplinary infrastructure projects. Its clients are Indian government institutions, road authorities, railways, municipal bodies and private entities, in India and overseas. The integrated delivery model brings engineering survey, DGPS and LiDAR mapping, geotechnical investigation, GIS and geospatial services, structural design, environmental and social impact assessment, land acquisition support, traffic studies and project management into a single structure, so clients deal with one accountable consultancy rather than coordinating several specialist vendors.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Land acquisition: 20-25% of order book, 12-36 months duration; DPR/road: 25-30%, 12-18 months; railway: 10-15%; geospatial: growing fast (property tax, river linking); water: Rs 13-14 Cr current, marine and river linking focus; private sector: ~30-40% of revenue, targeting Tata/Adani groups

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Railways:** Corridor and alignment planning, Final location surveys, Detailed engineering, Bridge and structure design, OHE and signalling layouts, GAD/ESP preparation for bridges and stations, DPRs for freight yards and terminals, Geotechnical investigation
- **Roads and Highways:** Master planning, Feasibility studies, Engineering surveys, Geotechnical investigations, Land acquisition support, Detailed project reports, Structural design, Traffic modelling, Project management
- **Geospatial:** Aerial and drone-based LiDAR, Mobile LiDAR, Terrestrial laser scanning, High-resolution GIS mapping, AI-based feature extraction, Digital twins, Land record digitisation
- **Urban Planning and Design:** Master planning, Transit-oriented development, Land-pooling schemes, 3D city modelling, Smart-city integration, Project management support

guidance.title: Guidance

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: International expansion (Riyadh outreach, pipeline for 2-3 countries); property taxation digitization for municipal bodies; digital twin product development (R&D with vendor); scaling geospatial services across 22 Indian states

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's infrastructure cycle has moved from periodic capex spurts to a sustained, policy-backed build-out; what matters for Monarch is the proportion of that spend passing through upstream, knowledge-intensive services - surveys, DPRs, geospatial intelligence, design and project management.
- Union Budget 2025-26 raised capital expenditure to Rs. 11.21 lakh crore, or 3.1% of GDP, and public capex has grown from approximately Rs. 2 lakh crore in FY15 to over Rs. 12 lakh crore in FY27 (BE).
- CRISIL projects nearly Rs. 143 lakh crore of infrastructure spending between FY24 and FY30, more than double the preceding seven years, with roughly Rs. 36.6 lakh crore earmarked for green investment.
- Roads and highways account for the largest near-term pipeline: MoRTH has outlined a PPP programme of approximately 13,400 km at an estimated cost of Rs. 8.3 lakh crore over the next three years, alongside 35 multimodal logistics parks under PPP involving around Rs. 46,000 crore of investment.
- Rail and metro will continue to generate demand for corridor planning, geotechnical work, final location surveys and multimodal integration, supported by near-complete electrification and continued investment in new lines, capacity augmentation, safety works and high-speed corridors.
- Urban infrastructure is under increasing pressure from mobility demand, water supply, drainage and land-use planning, driving investment in GIS-based planning, transit integration and network upgrades.
- Water and energy programmes generate steady demand for hydrology, network design, environmental and social impact studies and climate-resilient engineering, driven by flooding risk, wastewater regulation and renewable energy integration.
- GIS-led planning frameworks are pushing India to conceive infrastructure as interconnected networks rather than standalone assets, so corridor studies now combine urban impact, land systems, environmental and social assessment within a single scope - favouring firms that can combine surveys, design, geospatial intelligence, ESG and regulatory support in one delivery framework.
- PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan funding drove a significant share of this year's project awards, and those awards have grown more technically demanding.
- Mix shift: revenue is moving away from pure survey hours toward higher-yield, platform-based engineering and data services; revenue from operations grew 11.39% for the year ended 31 March 2026.
- Water Solutions work has moved from asset-mapping and localised pipe-routing toward river-basin modelling and coastal erosion infrastructure design, with margins in the segment holding up well; standardisation of GIS workflows cut manual data-processing time by 40%, freeing senior engineers for higher-value hydraulic advisory work.
- In the Energy segment, regulatory clearance is usually the more time-consuming element of an assignment rather than the engineering itself.
- Personnel costs rose in the near term to support the technology transition, but the same transition has reduced dependence on manual labour, which is expected to support operating margins over the medium term.
- Working-capital stress: debtor turnover extended to 113 days during the year, reflecting the billing cycles typical of public-sector contracts.
- The market the Company addresses is expected to reach USD 10.29 trillion by 2034 (7.02% CAGR), drawing in more competitors - domestic and larger global consultancies - all investing in LiDAR, digital twins and AI-based analytics; Monarch's constraint is scale rather than technical capability, since larger competitors can price more aggressively, absorb project delays more easily and invest faster in new technology.
- Talent is a second constraint: demand for BIM specialists, drone pilots, geospatial analysts, hydrologists and sustainability experts is outpacing supply, which directly affects how much work the Company can take on and deliver well.
- Land delays, environmental approvals, financing gaps and talent scarcity are described as real headwinds.
- Transportation (railways and highways) remains the principal segment, accounting for approximately 48% of the active order book - nearly half the order book in rail and highways.
- Secured a Rs. 13,000 lakh Northern Railway rate contract spanning 36 months, for engineering surveys and land acquisition management.
- Land acquisition and design consultancy for the Somnath-Dwarka Expressway packages in Gujarat exceeded Rs. 10,000 lakh in aggregate value.
- Undertook project management services for the upgrade of the Ghorpadi (Pune) and Wadi Bunder (Mumbai) depots under the Vande Bharat network.
- The Company's position going into FY27 rests on the order book, technical capability and balance sheet strength.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved from ~15% (FY23) to ~27.5% (H1FY26) due to in-house tech deployment (LiDAR, drones, digital modeling), reduced outsourcing, higher staff (630+), and QCDS-based tender wins (not pure L1); cost structure is project-dependent but tech-driven efficiency is structural

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds (Rs 93 Cr) allocated: Rs 12.5 Cr working capital by Mar’26, Rs 17.5 Cr capex by Mar’27, rest in FDs; no dividend policy yet; priority is growth, geographic expansion, and tech R&D; future dividends to be considered post-growth phase
